Electrosegura · MariaDB Integration Help

Type: SQL Database Connection (MariaDB/MySQL)

1) MariaDB Connection

Uses pyodbc library to connect to MariaDB/MySQL database containing sensor measurement data.

Standard connection_params (JSON):

{
  "driver": "MariaDB Unicode",
  "server": "185.14.56.58",
  "port": "4306",
  "database": "electrosegura_measurements",
  "uid": "electrosegura",
  "pwd": "your_password_here"
}

Required parameters:

  • driver: ODBC driver name (e.g., "MariaDB Unicode" or "MySQL ODBC 8.0 Driver")
  • server: Database server IP or hostname
  • port: Database port (default 3306 for MySQL, 4306 in this case)
  • database: Database name containing sensor data
  • uid: Database username
  • pwd: Database password

⚠️ Security Note

IMPORTANT: Store the password securely in the connection_params. Consider using environment variables or secure vault in production.

2) Available Procedures

A) Database Discovery (Recommended First Step)

Analyzes the MariaDB database and generates a comprehensive report of all available sensors:

  1. Scans all three tables - flow_data, reservoir_reading, water_quality
  2. Identifies unique sensor names - Groups sensors by name and type
  3. Generates configuration templates - Creates ready-to-use JSON configs
  4. Provides statistics - Date ranges, record counts, sensor distribution
  5. Exports results - JSON (detailed) and CSV (importable) formats

Output files:

  • JSON file: Complete discovery report with all details and statistics
  • CSV file: Easy-to-read table format for device and sensor creation

When to use: Run this procedure BEFORE creating any devices/sensors to understand your database structure.

B) Daily Sync (Scheduled)

Synchronizes sensor readings from MariaDB to Odoo:

  1. Build Device/Sensor Plan - Loads configured devices/sensors from Odoo with remotecontrol_params
  2. Fetch and Parse Rows - Queries MariaDB tables for new data since last sync
  3. Upsert Readings - Processes data and creates/updates readings in mdm.measurement.device.sensor.reading

When to use: Run this procedure AFTER creating devices and sensors to synchronize measurement data.

3) MariaDB Table Structure

Data is stored across three tables, each containing specific sensor types:

A) flow_data (caudal - Flow measurements)

time       : DATETIME - Reading timestamp
name       : VARCHAR  - Sensor name/identifier
flow       : FLOAT    - Flow value (m³/h or L/s)

B) reservoir_reading (volumen - Volume/Reservoir measurements)

time       : DATETIME - Reading timestamp
name       : VARCHAR  - Sensor name/identifier
volume     : FLOAT    - Volume/Level value (m³ or meters)

C) water_quality (calidad - Quality measurements)

time        : DATETIME - Reading timestamp
name        : VARCHAR  - Sensor name/identifier
conductance : FLOAT    - Conductance value (µS/cm)

4) Device Configuration

Each mdm.measurement.device needs remotecontrol_params (JSON) with device identifiers:

Required fields:

  • device_id: Device identifier (not used for MariaDB matching, but kept for consistency)

Optional fields:

  • start_date: Initial sync date (default: last reading or current year start)

Example device configuration:

{
  "device_id": "PARTIDOR 58",
  "start_date": "2025-01-01"
}

5) Sensor Configuration

Each mdm.measurement.device.sensor needs remotecontrol_params (JSON):

Required fields:

  • table: MariaDB table name to query (e.g. "flow_data", "nivel_partidor72_callosilla")
  • value_field: Column containing the numeric value (e.g. "flow", "nivel")
  • sensor_id: Exact value of the 'name' column in MariaDB for this sensor

Optional fields:

  • time_field: Timestamp column name (default: "time")
  • start_date: Initial sync date if no readings exist yet (default: Jan 1 of current year)

Example sensor configurations:

Flow sensor:
{
  "table": "flow_data",
  "value_field": "flow",
  "sensor_id": "Lo_Belmonte_Caudal"
}
Reservoir sensor:
{
  "table": "reservoir_reading",
  "value_field": "volume",
  "sensor_id": "Embalse_Callosilla"
}
Any other table (future-proof):
{
  "table": "nivel_partidor72_callosilla",
  "value_field": "nivel",
  "sensor_id": "Callosilla_Nivel",
  "start_date": "2025-01-01"
}

6) Data Processing Logic

Smart Sensor Matching

The system intelligently matches MariaDB data to Odoo sensors using:

  1. Type matching: sensor.remotecontrol_params.type determines which table to query
  2. Name matching: MariaDB 'name' column = sensor.remotecontrol_params.sensor_id
  3. Date range: Only fetches data after sensor's last reading or configured start_date

Multi-table Query Strategy

For each sensor type, the system:

  • Queries the appropriate table based on sensor type
  • Filters by sensor name and date range
  • Processes results and upserts into Odoo

7) Setup Workflow

  1. Configure connection: Set connection_params with server, database, credentials
  2. Test connection: Verify ODBC driver is installed (MariaDB Unicode or MySQL ODBC)
  3. RUN DISCOVERY: Execute "Database Discovery" procedure to analyze available sensors
  4. Review discovery report: Download JSON and CSV attachments to understand your data structure
  5. Create devices: Create mdm.measurement.device records based on discovery report
  6. Create sensors: Create mdm.measurement.device.sensor records with type and sensor_id from discovery report
  7. Test sync: Run "Daily Sync" procedure manually to verify configuration
  8. Schedule: Enable automatic scheduling if desired

Discovery Report Structure

JSON file contains:

{
  "executed_at": "2025-12-18 10:30:00",
  "connection_info": { ... },
  "devices_to_create": [
    {
      "sequence": 1,
      "name": "PARTIDOR 58",
      "suggested_odoo_name": "Partidor 58",
      "remotecontrol_params": {
        "device_id": "PARTIDOR 58",
        "start_date": "2025-01-01"
      }
    }
  ],
  "sensors_to_create": [
    {
      "sequence": 1,
      "device_sequence": 1,
      "device_name": "PARTIDOR 58",
      "suggested_odoo_name": "Caudal Partidor 58",
      "sensor_type": "caudal",
      "remotecontrol_params": {
        "type": "caudal",
        "sensor_id": "PARTIDOR 58",
        "start_date": "2025-01-01"
      }
    }
  ],
  "statistics": {
    "caudal": {
      "unique_sensors": 25,
      "date_range_start": "2025-01-01",
      "date_range_end": "2025-12-18",
      "total_readings": 125000
    }
  },
  "summary": {
    "total_unique_devices": 32,
    "total_sensors_to_create": 50
  }
}

CSV file contains: Easy-to-read tables for device and sensor creation with all necessary configuration.

8) Troubleshooting

Common Issues:

  • ODBC driver not found: Install MariaDB ODBC driver or MySQL ODBC driver on the server
  • Connection refused: Verify server IP, port, and firewall settings
  • Authentication failed: Check username and password in connection_params
  • No sensors found: Verify sensor_id in remotecontrol_params matches 'name' column exactly (case-sensitive)
  • Type mismatch: Ensure sensor type (caudal/volumen/calidad) matches available data
  • No data: Check start_date configuration and database table time range

Debugging:

Each procedure run creates audit attachments with detailed execution information and sample data for troubleshooting.

ODBC Driver Installation:

Ubuntu/Debian:

sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install unixodbc unixodbc-dev
sudo apt-get install odbc-mariadb
# or
sudo apt-get install libmyodbc

Verify driver installation:

odbcinst -q -d

import pyodbc from datetime import datetime
Remote = self.remote_id
discovery_result = { 'executed_at': fields.Datetime.now(), 'connection_info': {}, 'sensors_by_name': {}, 'devices_to_create': [], 'sensors_to_create': [], 'statistics': {}, 'errors': [] }
try: cfg = json.loads(Remote.connection_params or '{}') or {} driver = cfg.get('driver', 'MariaDB Unicode').strip() server = cfg.get('server', '').strip() port = cfg.get('port', '3306') database = cfg.get('database', '').strip() uid = cfg.get('uid', '').strip() pwd = cfg.get('pwd', '').strip()
if not all([server, database, uid]): raise Exception("Missing required connection parameters")
connection_string = ( "DRIVER={%s};" "SERVER=%s;" "PORT=%s;" "DATABASE=%s;" "UID=%s;" "PWD=%s;" ) % (driver, server, port, database, uid, pwd)
discovery_result['connection_info'] = { 'driver': driver, 'server': server, 'port': port, 'database': database, 'uid': uid }
conn = pyodbc.connect(connection_string) cursor = conn.cursor()
# Query similar to the example provided query = """ SELECT name, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT sensor_type ORDER BY sensor_type SEPARATOR ', ') AS sensor_types FROM ( SELECT name, 'flow_data|flow' AS sensor_type FROM flow_data WHERE TRIM(name) <> '' UNION SELECT name, 'reservoir_reading|volume' AS sensor_type FROM reservoir_reading WHERE TRIM(name) <> '' UNION SELECT name, 'water_quality|conductance' AS sensor_type FROM water_quality WHERE TRIM(name) <> '' ) t WHERE TRIM(name) <> '' GROUP BY name ORDER BY name """
cursor.execute(query) rows = cursor.fetchall()
device_counter = 1 sensor_counter = 1 total_sensors = 0
for row in rows: sensor_name = row[0] if row[0] else '' sensor_types = row[1] if row[1] else ''
if not sensor_name.strip(): continue
types_list = [t.strip() for t in sensor_types.split(',')] total_sensors += len(types_list)
# Information for analysis discovery_result['sensors_by_name'][sensor_name] = { 'sensor_types': types_list, 'sensor_count': len(types_list) }
# Device to create device_info = { 'sequence': device_counter, 'name': sensor_name, 'suggested_odoo_name': sensor_name.replace('_', ' ').title(), 'remotecontrol_params': { 'device_id': sensor_name, 'start_date': '2026-03-01' } } discovery_result['devices_to_create'].append(device_info)
# Sensors to create for this device (new format: table + value_field) for stype in types_list: # stype is 'flow_data|flow', 'reservoir_reading|volume', etc. parts = stype.split('|') table_name = parts[0].strip() value_field = parts[1].strip() if len(parts) > 1 else '' sensor_info = { 'sequence': sensor_counter, 'device_sequence': device_counter, 'device_name': sensor_name, 'suggested_odoo_name': '%s / %s' % ( sensor_name.replace('_', ' ').title(), table_name.replace('_', ' ').title() ), 'table': table_name, 'value_field': value_field, 'remotecontrol_params': { 'table': table_name, 'value_field': value_field, 'sensor_id': sensor_name, 'start_date': '2026-03-01' } } discovery_result['sensors_to_create'].append(sensor_info) sensor_counter += 1
device_counter += 1
# Gather additional statistics stats_queries = { 'flow_data': 'SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) as cnt, MIN(time) as min_date, MAX(time) as max_date, COUNT(*) as total_rows FROM flow_data WHERE TRIM(name) <> ""', 'reservoir_reading': 'SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) as cnt, MIN(time) as min_date, MAX(time) as max_date, COUNT(*) as total_rows FROM reservoir_reading WHERE TRIM(name) <> ""', 'water_quality': 'SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) as cnt, MIN(time) as min_date, MAX(time) as max_date, COUNT(*) as total_rows FROM water_quality WHERE TRIM(name) <> ""' }
for table_type, stats_query in stats_queries.items(): try: cursor.execute(stats_query) stat_row = cursor.fetchone() if stat_row: discovery_result['statistics'][table_type] = { 'unique_sensors': stat_row[0] or 0, 'date_range_start': str(stat_row[1]) if stat_row[1] else 'N/A', 'date_range_end': str(stat_row[2]) if stat_row[2] else 'N/A', 'total_readings': stat_row[3] or 0 } except Exception as e: discovery_result['errors'].append({ 'table': table_type, 'error': str(e) })
cursor.close() conn.close()
# Summary discovery_result['summary'] = { 'total_unique_devices': len(discovery_result['devices_to_create']), 'total_sensors_to_create': len(discovery_result['sensors_to_create']), 'sensors_by_table': { 'flow_data': sum(1 for s in discovery_result['sensors_to_create'] if s['table'] == 'flow_data'), 'reservoir_reading': sum(1 for s in discovery_result['sensors_to_create'] if s['table'] == 'reservoir_reading'), 'water_quality': sum(1 for s in discovery_result['sensors_to_create'] if s['table'] == 'water_quality'), } }
except Exception as ex: discovery_result['errors'].append({ 'fatal_error': str(ex), 'traceback': str(ex) })
# Create human-readable JSON discovery_json = json.dumps(discovery_result, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, default=str) discovery_b64 = base64.b64encode(discovery_json.encode('utf-8')) fname = 'electrosegura_discovery_%s.json' % fields.Datetime.now().replace(':', '').replace('-', '').replace(' ', '_')
att = env['ir.attachment'].create({ 'name': fname, 'datas_fname': fname, 'datas': discovery_b64, 'mimetype': 'application/json', 'res_model': 'remotecontrol', 'res_id': Remote.id })
# Also create a CSV for easy import csv_lines = [] csv_lines.append('Device Sequence,Device Name,Device Suggested Name,Device remotecontrol_params') for dev in discovery_result.get('devices_to_create', []): csv_lines.append('%s,"%s","%s","%s"' % ( dev['sequence'], dev['name'], dev['suggested_odoo_name'], json.dumps(dev['remotecontrol_params']) ))
csv_lines.append('') csv_lines.append('Sensor Sequence,Device Sequence,Device Name,Sensor Suggested Name,Table,Value Field,Sensor remotecontrol_params') for sens in discovery_result.get('sensors_to_create', []): csv_lines.append('%s,%s,"%s","%s",%s,%s,"%s"' % ( sens['sequence'], sens['device_sequence'], sens['device_name'], sens['suggested_odoo_name'], sens['table'], sens['value_field'], json.dumps(sens['remotecontrol_params']) ))
csv_content = '\n'.join(csv_lines) csv_b64 = base64.b64encode(csv_content.encode('utf-8')) csv_fname = 'electrosegura_discovery_%s.csv' % fields.Datetime.now().replace(':', '').replace('-', '').replace(' ', '_')
csv_att = env['ir.attachment'].create({ 'name': csv_fname, 'datas_fname': csv_fname, 'datas': csv_b64, 'mimetype': 'text/csv', 'res_model': 'remotecontrol', 'res_id': Remote.id })
summary = discovery_result.get('summary', {}) Remote.message_post( body='[Electrosegura] Discovery completed: %s devices, %s sensors (%s flow_data, %s reservoir_reading, %s water_quality)' % ( summary.get('total_unique_devices', 0), summary.get('total_sensors_to_create', 0), summary.get('sensors_by_table', {}).get('flow_data', 0), summary.get('sensors_by_table', {}).get('reservoir_reading', 0), summary.get('sensors_by_table', {}).get('water_quality', 0) ), attachment_ids=[att.id, csv_att.id] )
bag['electrosegura_discovery'] = discovery_result
